hunts.title: Root identity activity in AWS
hunts.hypothesis: A root principal should not create access keys, create users, or attach policies. Any root action outside a known break-glass window is worth an investigation.
hunts.query: any where cloud.provider:"aws" and user.name:"root" and event.action in ("ConsoleLogin", "CreateAccessKey", "CreateUser", "AttachUserPolicy")
hunts.finding: 4 root events across 4 actions: ConsoleLogin x1, CreateAccessKey x1, AttachUserPolicy x1, CreateUser x1.
hunts.detection_change: Alert on root CreateAccessKey, CreateUser, AttachUserPolicy, and ConsoleLogin. Require a break-glass ticket, and export the finding to Apsis so the IAM graph can show which paths the new principal can reach.
hunts.limitations: Synthetic root-compromise scenario. A production rule needs a break-glass allowlist and an approved source-IP or identity-provider context.

hunts.title: Service binary outside a trusted path
hunts.hypothesis: A new service should run from a signed system or application path. A service binary in a user-writable directory, or a shell command as the service image, is a persistence lead.
hunts.query: any where event.code:"7045" and winlog.event_data.ImagePath like~ ("*\\Users\\Public\\*", "*\\AppData\\*", "*\\Temp\\*", "*\\ProgramData\\*", "*cmd.exe*", "*powershell*")
hunts.finding: 1 service installs matched the heuristic: UpdaterSvc.
hunts.detection_change: The existing rule covers user-writable service paths. Add a software-inventory allowlist, alert on 7045 from non-admin users, and compare the service name with the installed product.
hunts.limitations: PSEXESVC is not flagged by the path heuristic because it runs from C:\Windows. The existing rule catches it by name, which is why hunts and rules are complementary.

hunts.title: DNS tunneling pattern
hunts.hypothesis: A high volume of unique, long subdomains under one parent domain can indicate data encoded in DNS queries.
hunts.query: any where event.action:"dns_query" and dns.question.name like~ "*.tunnel.example"
hunts.finding: 25 queries under tunnel.example, 25 unique subdomains, longest label 38 characters.
hunts.detection_change: Add a DNS tunneling rule that scores parent-domain rarity, unique subdomain count, and label length. Exclude known CDN, telemetry, and mail domains.
hunts.limitations: Synthetic labels are regular and deliberately easy to spot. A production hunt needs entropy estimates, baseline parent-domain frequency, and resolver context.

hunts.title: LSASS access from a user-writable path
hunts.hypothesis: A process outside System32 or SysWOW64 should not open LSASS with credential-dumping access. This is a hunt for credential theft that is independent of the existing rule.
hunts.query: any where event.code:"10" and winlog.event_data.TargetImage:"*lsass.exe" and not winlog.event_data.SourceImage like~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\*", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*")
hunts.finding: 1 LSASS access events came from a user-writable path.
hunts.detection_change: The existing rule catches this path. Add a hunt for LSASS access from user-writable directories, and compare the process signer and parent with the rule verdict.
hunts.limitations: Security products and diagnostic tools may legitimately access LSASS. Require signer, parent, and change-ticket context before calling it malicious.
